meta.title: PortPress Demo
meta.description: A guided demo for importing static source files into WordPress and exporting WordPress as static HTML.
meta.author: Adam Zielinski

files.README.md:
# PortPress Sample Repository

This README.md is the first file to import in the PortPress demo.

It shows how static source material can become reviewable WordPress content before anything is published.

## Try this first

1. Open Tools -> Universal Importer.
2. Paste the demo source folder path.
3. Run a dry run, then run the import.

docs.launch-plan.md:
# Launch Plan

- Import the source folder into WordPress drafts.
- Review converted blocks and internal links.
- Export the WordPress site as static HTML.
docs.publishing-notes.txt: Plain text files are accepted too. PortPress keeps them inspectable instead of ignoring useful source material.

site.index.html:
Static HTML Source

This HTML file is here to show that PortPress can import ordinary rendered documents alongside Markdown.

Internal source links should be reviewed before publishing.

steps.command:
wp post create --post_type=page --post_status=publish --post_title='About the PortPress Demo' --post_name=about-portpress-demo --post_content='

About the PortPress Demo

This page gives the static exporter a normal WordPress page to crawl and package.

  • Imported drafts can be reviewed before publishing.
  • Published pages can be exported as static HTML.
  • Same-site links and assets are rewritten for portable hosting.
'

wp post create --post_type=page --post_status=publish --post_title='Static Hosting Checklist' --post_name=static-hosting-checklist --post_content='

Static Hosting Checklist

After downloading the ZIP, extract it and preview the folder over local HTTP before hosting it.

Check the homepage, dated posts, page links, CSS, images, and any JavaScript that expects HTTP instead of file URLs.

'
